neighbours.label: the token ' chap' (chapel, chap., old chap) and the piece after word-initial 'ch' in chlor- / chol- words (ch|lo|rella, cholesterol)
fire: Behind the castle stand a tiny chapel and a walled garden.
The argument is set out more fully in chap. 4 of the second volume.
Our neighbour is a cheerful chap who repairs clocks for a living.
The village has a stone chapel that dates from the twelfth century.
The pool smelled strongly of chlorine after it was cleaned.
Leaves are green because they contain chlorophyll.
Her doctor said her cholesterol was a little too high.
An outbreak of cholera closed the port for most of the summer.
